description:
FILED s535a (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08) from a span-port neighbour probe (scratch/s535a/pr/q02.pl).  PRE-EXISTING (main 06a4b8ba); the span pass is not involved -- this is the DECLARATION LOWERING.

REPRODUCER (probed vs perl 5.40.3):

    sub f { my $n = shift; my $c = my $d = $n; f($n - 1) if $n > 0; "$c/$d" }
    print f(2), "\n";
    my @s; for my $i (1 .. 2) { my $a2 = my $b2 = $i; push @s, sub { $b2 } }
    print join(",", map { $_->() } @s), "\n";

perl:              2/2 / 1,2
main 06a4b8ba:     2/0 / 2,2      -- SILENT WRONG: the CHAINED declarator `my $d` is not a per-call / per-iteration lexical

WHY (read, s535a): a scalar `my $c = my $d = EXPR` lowers through the single-scalar branch of _lower_decl_stmt: `$c` gets its `let`, and the initializer `my $d = EXPR` goes to the expression compiler, which lowers the inner `my` as a plain assignment `(p-scalar-= $d EXPR)` to a symbol nobody let-binds -- one shared cell (at file level the forward-declared package global).  The list / container chain (`my @c = my @d = …`) has its own arm (Pl::Stmt::decl_chain) that let-binds every name; the scalar chain does not reach it.  A recursion or a closure in a loop then shares one `$d`.

FIX DIRECTION: route a scalar decl whose initializer is a chain through the decl_chain arm (or let-bind the chained names around the declaration, as #3431's embedded-my let does), keeping a PROMOTED chained name (the span pass's `_emb_promoted`, #4425) on its cell.  Probe the file-level and flattened-block forms (Pl/t/span-binder-01.t rows 1-3) as the guard.

=== DONE (s536d) ===
FIXED (Opus 5.5, 2026-11-08; worktree agent-a481004870e7c115b, commit "s536d WIP: #4544 ..."; generation v2-12400).
MECHANISM: `_decl_init_embedded_my_names` excluded every declarator at the statement's OWN level, so a SCALAR chain `my $c = my $d = EXPR` -- lowered by the scalar arm as `my $c = <expression>` -- left `my $d` to the expression compiler: `(p-scalar-= $d …)` on the forward-declared cell.  Now the own-level exclusion keeps only the LEADING declarator for a scalar declaration (`Pl::Stmt::single_scalar_decl`), so a chained `my` is an expression-embedded `my` and takes #3431's let (fresh per execution).  The symbols are ONE reading, `_decl_init_embedded_my_syms`, which the capture promoter's `_embedded_decl_candidates` now also reads for a declaration -- so a chained / embedded declarator a nested NAMED sub captures is promoted (requalify-binder-01.t #3801 rows), and the pre-existing refusal "possibly captured by nested sub" for `sub run { my $l = id(my $t = 1); … sub g { ++$t } … }` is gone.
PROBES (scratch/s536d/pr/a1 a2 a5 in the worktree): recursion 2/2, closures per iteration 11,22,33 / 30,60, tail value, chained container `my $c = my @d`, chained hash, conditional init, `\$d` distinct per call, string eval, file-level + nested named sub -- all = perl; a2 row 10 is #4641 (the file-level veto, pre-existing).
GUARD: Pl/t/while-my-closure-01.t rows 6 + 7 (fail on the base extraction).
CORPUS-DIFF: closure.t (`my $a = bless \my $dummy, "trace"`: `$dummy` now let-bound per call) and substr.t (`my $x = my $y = "AB"` in a loop).
subject: SILENT WRONG: the CHAINED scalar declarator of `my $c = my $d = EXPR` is not a lexical -- one shared cell across recursive calls and loop iterations (pre-existing, the declaration lowering)
